answers.answer:
No. SCOPe 2.08 (stable, released 2021-09-22) does not support treating these three groups as one homologous superfamily. It places them in one fold but in three separate superfamilies, and SCOPe asserts homology only at the superfamily level and below.

Verified SCOPe 2.08 facts:
- Fold f.21 (sunid 81344), 'Heme-binding four-helical bundle', class f (Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides). Fold comment: 'core: four transmembrane helices, up-and-down bundle, binds one or two heme groups in between the helices'. The fold's homology section reports homology_implied_by_level = false with the warning 'SCOPe levels above superfamily do not imply homology'.
- The fold has exactly three child superfamilies, each with homology_implied_by_level = true at scope 'sf' (i.e. homology is asserted only within each superfamily):
  1. f.21.1 (sunid 81342) 'Transmembrane di-heme cytochromes', families f.21.1.1 Formate dehydrogenase N cytochrome (gamma) subunit, f.21.1.2 Cytochrome b of cytochrome bc1 complex, and f.21.1.0 automated matches. Comment: 'Three of the four heme-ligands are conserved between the two families; both heme groups bind similarly but not identically'.
  2. f.21.2 (sunid 81343) 'Fumarate reductase respiratory complex transmembrane subunits', families f.21.2.1 FrdC cytochrome b subunit and f.21.2.2 SdhC/FrdC and SdhD/FrdD subunits. Comment: 'two distinct families: in one family the common fold is contained in a single-chain subunit, in the other it is formed by two chains'.
  3. f.21.3 (sunid 103501) 'Respiratory nitrate reductase 1 gamma chain', single family f.21.3.1 (e.g. domains d1q16c_, d1y4zc_, d1siwc_ from E. coli nitrate reductase A).
